correctness.rationale: For every \(q=2^m\) and \(u\ne0\), the cubic \(f=T^3+aT^2+bT+c\) depresses under \(T=Y+a\) to \((B,C)=(b+a^2,c+ab)\), while its affine shift depresses to \((B+u,C+ua+v)\). The coefficient map \((a,b,c)\mapsto(B,C,C+ua+v)\) is a bijection. For the depressed cubic, \(C=0\) is exactly the nonsquarefree locus. Carmon (2014), Section 2, gives the Berlekamp expression \(1+B^3/C^2\) and the characteristic-two Pellet identity; hence \(S(0)=\varepsilon(q-1)\) and \(S(B)=-\varepsilon\) for \(B\ne0\), with \(\varepsilon=(-1)^{m+1}\). The shifted correlation \(\sum_B S(B)S(B+u)=-q\) follows exactly, all marginal sign sums vanish, and expanding yields all nine joint counts including \(q=2\). A standalone root-and-derivative enumeration checks 352 shifts and 3,765,008 polynomial pairs over six binary fields, without using the Berlekamp formula. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The complete nine-cell Möbius-sign joint distribution is a natural exact fixed-degree Chowla-type invariant including nonsquarefree failures. It is uniform across every binary finite field and every nonconstant affine shift, and yields the sharp negative signed correlation \(-q\), far more precise than a general asymptotic cancellation bound. The sign-resolved classification is not implied by earlier unsigned squarefree counts; its number-theoretic interest does not rest on computing code or an unproved downstream conjecture.
